operator_io_quirks: Ingredient/Recipe/Nutrition/Quantity are mixed-case table names; all identifiers must be double-quoted in generated SQL.

Quantity.recipe_id has TWO FK parents (Nutrition.recipe_id and Recipe.recipe_id); pragma foreign_key_list returns both, schema.fks dict keyed by (child_t,child_c) keeps only one -> the other is silently lost.
Nutrition.recipe_id is PK and FK to Recipe.recipe_id; Recipe has 1031 rows, Nutrition 878 -> FK parent set is a strict subset, not all Recipe ids appear in Nutrition.
Quantity.recipe_id null_rate 0.005 and ingredient_id null_rate 0.005: FK columns are nullable, so NULL FK values are legal and present.
All columns notnull=0 (pragma reports 0 even for PKs); NOT NULL is not enforced by sqlite here, so TS insert failures are rare.
Ingredient.plural has 78% NULL and only 3 distinct values ('s','es','#NAME?'); '#NAME?' is an Excel error string stored as text.
Recipe.title null_rate 0.148, distinct 878 < 1031 rows: title is NOT unique despite looking name-like.
Recipe.servings/prep_min/cook_min/stnd_min all share null_rate 0.148 (same 152 rows missing) - correlated nulls, not independent.
Nutrition REAL columns have 0 nulls and distinct counts 51..864; alcohol has only 51 distinct (mostly 0.0) - heavy zero mass.
Quantity.max_qty and min_qty have identical distinct=62 and identical samples: they are near-duplicates (min==max in samples).
Quantity.optional has 2 distinct values 'TRUE'/'FALSE' stored as TEXT, not INTEGER/BOOL.
Recipe.intro/directions are long free text truncated in samples; String fuzzer length range will be [min,max+1] of these, potentially large.
operator_ts_expectations: All PK columns (ingredient_id, recipe_id, quantity_id) dispatch to Number fuzzer with scale=0 -> integers in [-1,1] then perturbed by +-1/+-2; tiny range, so PK collisions are frequent and sample_fresh_primary_keys drops many rows.

Number fuzzer for REAL columns (protein, carbo, ...) uses scale=0 (no args in 'REAL') -> range [-1,1] floats, wildly implausible vs original 0..2738 (vitamin_a); drives FN on range predicates like 'vitamin_a > 500'.

String fuzzer for TEXT columns draws from CHARSET a-zA-Z 0-9() with length [0,20] default (no length arg in TEXT) -> 'category'/'unit' values become random gibberish; implausible for equality predicates on 'dairy','cup(s)' -> FN.
String fuzzer contaminate (0.5) appends/prefixes random chars -> even literal-pool values get corrupted, breaking equality joins on category/unit.

FK fill: Quantity.recipe_id draws from parent's FINAL filtered values; Nutrition has only 878 rows and PK filtering may shrink further, so many Quantity rows get NULL or duplicate recipe_id -> join cardinality mismatch vs original (FP/FN on COUNT).
Quantity.recipe_id has two FK parents; whichever the dict keeps wins, the other parent's referential integrity is not enforced -> dangling recipe_ids possible (FP on join).

Nutrition.recipe_id PK is also FK to Recipe; TS generates it as a Number PK (fresh) AND as FK child - upstream draws FK from parent, so Nutrition.recipe_id values are Recipe ids, but PK dedup may drop rows -> Nutrition smaller than Recipe, matching original shape by luck.
Recipe.title is not unique but TS does not know; String fuzzer may produce duplicates -> title-based joins get extra rows (FP).
Quantity.optional 'TRUE'/'FALSE' as TEXT: String fuzzer produces random strings, so 'optional = TRUE' predicates match nothing -> FN.
alcohol mostly 0.0: Number fuzzer uniform [-1,1] rarely hits exactly 0.0 -> 'alcohol = 0' predicates FN.
servings/prep_min/cook_min/stnd_min correlated nulls: TS fills each independently, so the 0.148 co-null pattern is destroyed -> queries filtering on multiple being NULL together FN.
max_qty==min_qty in samples: TS generates them independently -> 'max_qty = min_qty' predicates FN.
